configuration.CLI: python3 app.py --data <existing local data dir> --general-chat-config <administrator JSON path>
configuration.excluded: Secret values, endpoints, headers, alternate transport, test_only and all unknown/duplicate fields are rejected. Symlink, non-regular, oversized or group/world-writable configuration is rejected with a value-free error.
configuration.credential_boundary: Configuration load, build, preview and approval read no key. Only the existing adapter operation invokes the lazy injected supplier; default supplier accesses only Anthropic_KEY at that time. No .env file is auto-loaded or read by this implementation/task.
configuration.default_off: No configuration or enabled=false returns no general runtime and no credential/network access. Existing legacy runtime is preserved. An enabled actual general connection and legacy chat_configuration are explicitly incompatible; prior fixture/loopback combinations remain supported.
configuration.verification_label: Runtime availability means configured ability to request execution. account_verified=false and billing_verified=false; actual account/model access, paid billing and production readiness remain unverified.

changed_behavior.detail: Closed-schema startup contract/factory, mutually exclusive general sources, no dual live legacy ledger, workspace check before recovery, optional CLI configuration. Standard launch remains disconnected.

Three unconditional non-test layers become validated trusted activation checks. Exact production bounded types, no custom opener/endpoint, pinned adapter/supplier/transports, model/price/connection revision and activation hash remain bound. No SDK or new send runtime.

Only exact actual LiveTransport + exact AnthropicChatAdapter + current owned active operation + exact sanitized ProposalError category=credentials proves adapter provider transport not entered. Its current sending attempt becomes not_sent via the official ledger API and its current hold is released. Remote/timeout/model/billing/unknown failures retain uncertainty. Lost ownership cannot upgrade a prior unknown attempt.

Public count/message not_sent and actionable key-reset/new-consent guidance distinguish known non-submission. Earlier observed model response/usage and costs take precedence and remain preserved; a persistent submitted flag alone does not decide the current attempt.

Root-authorized cooperating worker added owned sending→not_sent finish_attempt support and common exposure protection for failed usage journal persistence. This worker did not edit ledger.py or existing tests; final integrated ledger hash is recorded.

budget_integration: New crossflow tests use actual HTTP media_action_decide execute and general_chat_decide controllers and the real project:<pid> budget. Image admission reserves .01 and blocks chat admission; a chat reservation blocks image admission. No rehearsal-scope injection, second reservation or provider dispatch. Concurrent conversation admission also has one budget winner.

credential_boundary_before.observed: Before the not_sent change, missing count key already released its hold but recorded attempt unknown; missing message key after successful count left reservation uncertain/attempt unknown/live_model_called null. This is the measured baseline. Initial expectation that count itself retained uncertain was wrong and remains in credential-before.log.

credential_boundary_after: None, empty and exception suppliers are lazy until approved execution and create no adapter provider request. Current count or message attempt is not_sent; the current reservation is cancelled, live_model_called=false if no earlier response exists, and fresh explicit consent can succeed after fixing settings. If a prior round has observed usage, its estimated60 and live_model_called=true remain; only the later unsubmitted reservation is released.

preserved_failures.reason: Initial expected state assumed count credentials failure held uncertain. Actual code already released count hold; measured baseline was corrected and preserved separately.

Initial test expected typed production_tool budget rejection to be blocked, but the existing tool collapses that case to invalid_arguments. The final integration tests use the actual creator UI media controller, which returns HTTP400 with budget reason. Product tool classification was not changed or hidden.

before_after_evidence.preservation: Existing app.py/chat_general.py text was captured before modifications. Source changes are additions/targeted gate and failure-state replacements; no reset/stash/commit/head copy, unrelated code deletion or other-worker edit reversal.

known_limits: Actual provider entitlement, region/key/billing identity and live usage shapes were not tested. An administrator connection ID/revision is a declaration, not proof of the account.

Actual-mode usage remains strict: missing/null/unknown/nonzero unsupported dimensions are not zero and do not allow tools. Standard supported observations are estimates, not invoices. Request-bound trusted general-chat billing reconciliation remains a separate incomplete capability.
No authentication/team production promotion: the application remains its existing local single-owner boundary. No deployment, operational data change or production-readiness acceptance occurred.

The same-user trusted startup and injected supplier remain server authority. A supplier is expected to acquire credentials only. The new not_sent classification proves the exact adapter did not delegate to its provider transport; it is not a claim about arbitrary side effects inside unrelated trusted Python code.
Existing raw-DB metadata corruption/preflight limitation is unchanged; no audio parser or media fallback expansion was included.
